title: Theo and the Cipher
premise: Estate lawyer Bram Thackeray is handed a will for a man who died decades ago — signed, witnessed, and filed the day after his funeral. When a confession letter arrives in the same postmark, Bram discovers the will's clauses are a cipher pointing to a ledger of crimes committed by the town's founding families. As Bram decodes it with help from the dead man's estranged granddaughter and a retired archivist who remembers too much, they realize someone is killing off the witnesses named in the ledger. The story ends when Bram exposes the ledger at a public reading of the will, forcing the last living conspirator — the town's beloved judge — to confess before he can silence them.
about_author: Rosalind Galloway spent fifteen years as a probate clerk in coastal Maine before turning to fiction, and her mysteries are known for their forensic attention to paperwork and inheritance law. She lives in a converted lighthouse keeper's cottage with two indifferent cats and an ever-growing archive of real estate deeds she swears are 'for research.'

chapters.title: The Will That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Bram Thackeray, POV. A courier delivers a sealed will for Edmund Voss, dead fifty-two years, postmarked the day after his funeral. Bram's professional skepticism wars with fascination as the document's paper proves genuinely aged. Emotional beat: unease — the first crack in Bram's belief that every death can be neatly filed.

chapters.title: Postmark Yesterday
chapters.summary: Bram, POV. A confession letter arrives, unsigned, claiming Edmund Voss was murdered and that 'the ledger remembers what the town forgot.' Bram visits the records office and finds Voss's death certificate suspiciously clean. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into resolve; Bram decides to open the will against protocol.

chapters.title: Clauses Like Teeth
chapters.summary: Bram, POV. Reading the will aloud alone, Bram notices recurring odd phrasings — dates out of order, initials embedded in bequests. A pattern emerges: the will is a cipher. Emotional beat: intellectual thrill curdling as Bram realizes whoever wrote this expected a reader to die for finding it.

chapters.title: The Granddaughter Who Never Knew Him
chapters.summary: Iris Voss, POV. Iris, a night-shift nurse estranged from her family's history, receives notice she's named in a will for a grandfather she thought abandoned her mother. She arrives in town angry and curious. Emotional beat: guarded grief; the ache of inherited secrets.

chapters.title: Two Keys, One Lock
chapters.summary: Bram, POV. Bram meets Iris, legally obligated to inform her of her bequest: a key to a safe-deposit box that no bank in town admits exists. They distrust each other but agree to compare notes. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance, two lonely people circling the same wound.

chapters.title: What Mrs. Aldous Kept
chapters.summary: Retired archivist Winnifred Aldous, POV. Winnifred recognizes the will's phrasing from documents she catalogued in the 1970s and quietly pulls the originals before anyone else can. She reveals the founding families' charitable trust hid land fraud and a drowned laborer no one investigated. Emotional beat: guilt of the complicit bystander, finally choosing a side.

chapters.title: The Ledger in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: Bram, POV. Following the cipher, Bram realizes the 'ledger' is the memorial plaque in the town square — names, dates, and donations encoding transactions. Photographing it, Bram notices a car following them. Emotional beat: paranoia arriving; the past is not resting.

chapters.title: First to Fall
chapters.summary: Iris, POV. The retired police sergeant who signed Voss's death certificate is found dead in an apparent fall. Iris connects him to the will's witness list. Emotional beat: horror made personal — the cipher isn't history, it's a hit list being worked in order.

chapters.title: Reading the Dead Man's Hand
chapters.summary: Bram, POV. Decoding faster now, Bram learns Edmund Voss was the bookkeeper for the conspiracy and turned state's evidence secretly before dying — or was killed to prevent it. The letter's author claims to have been his accomplice. Emotional beat: moral vertigo; justice and crime share a handwriting.

chapters.title: The Bank That Forgot
chapters.summary: Bram and Iris, alternating POV. They trace the phantom safe-deposit box to a shuttered branch and find the box empty except for one item: a photograph of the four original conspirators, one face scratched out. Emotional beat: intimacy of shared danger; Iris and Bram stop pretending this is just legal work.

chapters.title: Winnifred's Warning
chapters.summary: Winnifred, POV. Winnifred identifies the scratched-out face as young Judge Harlan Pike, now the town's revered elder statesman. Before she can deliver her full file, her archive office is ransacked. Emotional beat: fear of the institution itself; the law may be the enemy.

chapters.title: A Funeral for a Living Man
chapters.summary: Bram, POV. Bram attends Judge Pike's public tribute and watches him work the crowd, realizing Pike has been quietly buying up the heirs' debts for years — leverage disguised as charity. Emotional beat: cold clarity; the killer hides inside respectability.

chapters.title: The Second Letter
chapters.summary: Iris, POV. Another letter arrives, this one addressed to Iris: her grandmother helped Voss hide the ledger and paid for it with exile. Iris learns her family's poverty was punishment, not failure. Emotional beat: rage transmuted into purpose; the found-family bond between Iris, Bram, and Winnifred solidifies.

chapters.title: Broken Cipher, Broken Trust
chapters.summary: Bram, POV. A break-in at Bram's office steals the decoded pages; only Winnifred's memory and Iris's photographs survive. Bram suspects a leak — the courier? the clerk? Emotional beat: betrayal and isolation; the trio must decide how much to trust even each other.

chapters.title: The Drowned Laborer's Daughter
chapters.summary: New voice: Maren Oduya, POV. An elderly woman contacts Bram: her father was the drowned laborer, and she has kept Voss's final letter for fifty years on his instruction to wait 'until someone reads the stone.' Emotional beat: grief honored at last; the victims step out of the ledger and become people.

chapters.title: Counting Down the Witness List
chapters.summary: Bram, POV. Cross-referencing the cipher with recent deaths, Bram finds only three names left — themselves included. They request police protection and are politely refused by a department Pike helped fund. Emotional beat: claustrophobic urgency; the clock is audible now.

chapters.title: Trap at the Trust
chapters.summary: Iris, POV. The trio stages a fake decoding session at the charitable trust's offices to flush out the mole. It works — and the mole is Bram's own junior partner, blackmailed over an old mistake. Emotional beat: pity tangled with anger; coercion, not evil, built the conspiracy's long arm.

chapters.title: What the Judge Buried
chapters.summary: Bram, POV. Confronted, the junior partner reveals Pike keeps his insurance in a private vault beneath the courthouse — and that Pike plans to amend the trust charter at Friday's ceremony, legally destroying the evidence forever. Emotional beat: cornered-animal determination; they must strike in public or not at all.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: Bram, POV. At the charter ceremony, Bram invokes an obscure probate statute to publicly read the Voss will — the cipher aloud, clause by clause, while Iris projects the plaque's decoded ledger behind the podium. Emotional beat: triumphant terror; the room turns from celebration to reckoning.

chapters.title: Confession, Postmarked Fifty Years Late
chapters.summary: Judge Pike, POV. Cornered before the town, Pike unravels — revealing he wrote both letters himself, unable to die with Voss's murder unpunished by anyone but him, then chose to protect the secret anyway. He confesses on record. Emotional beat: tragic collapse; the villain wanted to be caught all along and couldn't allow it.

chapters.title: Probate of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Bram, POV. In the aftermath, the courts reopen the Voss case; the drowned laborer gets a headstone with his true name. Bram resigns from the firm to practice estate law for families like the Oduyas. Emotional beat: bittersweet restoration; justice arrived late but arrived.

chapters.title: Theo and the Cipher
chapters.summary: Iris, POV. Iris finally opens the box's false bottom and finds Voss's letter to his unborn granddaughter — Theo, the name her mother never used — asking forgiveness and leaving her the truth instead of money. The found family shares dinner above the old archive. Emotional beat: quiet peace; memory, once decoded, becomes inheritance.
